documents.title: Physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I never rebooked my physical from last fall, sorry. I'm home until at least the summer now. Any openings in early April? Mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Henry, you're booked for Tuesday April 4 at 8:20. Please come fasting if you can, the doctor will likely order bloodwork.

results.text: Reactive. HIV-1 antibody positive on supplemental differentiation assay; HIV-2 antibody negative.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33M, physical, last seen 9/2021. Home since winter, planning his next posting for later in the year. Feels well. No fevers, weight steady, no cough. Sleeping fine. Running 3x a week.

No meds. NKDA. Still not smoking, no alcohol.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: Vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing. Oropharynx clear, no thrush. No cervical, axillary or inguinal adenopathy. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no spleen tip. Skin clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
- Routine labs: CBC, CMP, lipids.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening recommended for all adults; he agrees. Added to today's draw.
- Vaccines: Tdap 2021, flu given last fall. Will review others once labs are back.
- RTC 1 yr.

orders.reason: new HIV diagnosis, baseline before TB testing

documents.title: Result discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt directly with the HIV screen: 4th generation test reactive, confirmed HIV-1 on the differentiation assay. HCV antibody negative. Other labs from the physical normal.

He was quiet at first, then had good questions. Explained that this is a treatable chronic infection, that most people on one pill a day reach an undetectable level and live a normal lifespan, and that undetectable means no sexual transmission. He is not in a relationship now; advised condoms and informing any recent partners, offered help with partner notification through the health department, he will think about it.

Plan: baseline labs tomorrow (CD4, viral load, genotype, hep B serologies, RPR), TB skin test placed Monday and read Wednesday, chest film Wednesday. Office visit 4/21 to go over everything and start treatment. Will also set up Infectious Disease. He knows to call before then with any questions; gave him my cell.

results.text: No major resistance mutations detected in reverse transcriptase, protease or integrase. Susceptible to all integrase inhibitors and NRTIs tested.

documents.title: Baseline HIV labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CD4 350, viral load 55,000. Hep B surface antigen negative, surface antibody positive (vaccinated, immune). RPR nonreactive. Genotype still pending. Will review all at the 4/21 visit.

documents.title: Questions before my visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: A few questions for the 21st so I don't forget: will I be on this for life, can I still travel for work, and is there anything I should avoid until I start the medicine? Also do I need to tell my employer?

documents.title: RE: Questions before my visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All good questions and we'll go through each one on the 21st. Short answers: treatment is long term, yes you can keep working and traveling once things are settled, and no, you are not required to tell your employer. Nothing to avoid before the visit. Write down anything else that comes up.

documents.title: PPD placement
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Tuberculin 5 TU placed intradermally L volar forearm, good wheal raised. No prior positive test per pt; never had BCG that he knows of. Return Wednesday morning for the read.

documents.title: PPD read
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Read at 48 hours: 7 mm of induration, measured transversely, L forearm. Some faint redness beyond the edge, not counted. With his new HIV diagnosis this counts as a positive test. Routed to PCP. Pt walked to radiology for his chest film after the read.

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. No prior studies. Heart size and mediastinal contours are within normal limits. No hilar or mediastinal lymph node enlargement. Lungs are clear without consolidation, nodule, cavitation or upper lobe scarring. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: No radiographic evidence of active or prior pulmonary tuberculosis. Normal chest.

medications.drug: bictegravir 50 MG / emtricitabine 200 MG / tenofovir alafenamide 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily
Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily for 9 months
Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily while taking isoniazid

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: new HIV
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33M here to go over his new HIV result and start treatment. Screen from his 4/4 physical was reactive and confirmed as HIV-1 by differentiation.

He has had time to read. No symptoms: denies cough, fevers, sweats at night or any weight change. No sores, rashes, swallowing trouble or diarrhea. Today he told me he injected drugs for a stretch in his early twenties, shared equipment at times, has not used in many years and has no cravings; he had not mentioned it before. No current partner. Mood ok, has told one close friend.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: comfortable. No thrush or oral lesions. No lymphadenopathy. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin without lesions. Neuro nonfocal. Exam unremarkable.

Data:
- CD4 350, HIV RNA 55,000 copies/mL (4/7)
- Genotype: no major resistance mutations
- HBsAg neg, HBsAb pos (immune); HCV Ab neg; RPR nonreactive
- CMP, CBC, lipids from 4/4 normal
- PPD 7 mm at 48 h (4/19), positive for someone with HIV
- CXR 4/19: clear, nothing to suggest active TB

A/P
1. HIV-1 infection, new, CD4 350, no opportunistic infection. Start bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide one tablet daily today; no resistance, hep B immune, renal function normal. Talked through taking it at the same time every day, what to do with a missed dose, and that most people suppress within a few months. Not yet at a CD4 level that calls for PJP prophylaxis. Referral to Infectious Disease for co-management; I will keep doing his primary care. Viral load and CD4 again in about 8 weeks.
2. Latent TB infection: positive PPD, no symptoms, clear film. Isoniazid 300 mg daily for 9 months with pyridoxine 50 mg. No interaction concern with his ART. Monthly symptom check and LFTs for now; told him to stop and call for nausea, dark urine, yellow eyes or numb feet.
3. Past injection drug use, remote: no current use. Naloxone not needed per his account; he declines. Will revisit.
4. Vaccines: PCV20 and first MenACWY today. Second MenACWY in 8 weeks. Flu in the fall.
5. Prevention counseling, condoms, partner services info given again.
RTC 3 months, sooner for any problem.

documents.title: Prior authorization approved
documents.author: RN
documents.body: MassHealth prior auth for bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide approved through 4/2024. Pharmacy had dispensed a 3-day emergency supply Friday; full 30-day fill picked up today along with isoniazid and B6. Pt aware.

documents.title: Infectious Disease consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/16/2023
Referring: primary care

Thank you for referring Mr. Dabrowski, 33, newly diagnosed HIV-1 on screening, baseline CD4 350 and viral load 55,000, no resistance on genotype. Started on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 4/21 with isoniazid and pyridoxine for latent TB (PPD 7 mm, clear chest film).

He reports taking every dose so far, no side effects beyond mild loose stools the first week, now resolved. No symptoms of active TB.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: well, no thrush, no adenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly, skin clear.

Impression and plan:
1. HIV-1, early on ART, tolerating well. Agree with regimen. VL and CD4 at 8 weeks, then every 3 months until suppressed. Ok to draw at your office.
2. LTBI on 9 months INH. Please continue monthly LFTs while on INH.
3. Hep B immune, no need for vaccination. Hep A and zoster vaccination can be discussed at a later visit.
4. Follow up here in 3 months.

We appreciate being involved in his care.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Henry, your liver tests a month into isoniazid are normal. Keep going with both pills. Next check is when you come in for the second meningitis shot in June.

documents.title: RE: Liver tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. ID doctor was great btw. All good here.

documents.title: Vaccine and lab draw
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second MenACWY given L deltoid. Drew LFTs, CD4 and viral load as ordered. INH symptom check: no nausea, no abdominal pain, no dark urine, no tingling in hands or feet. Taking all three meds daily per pt. Mentions he is heading out west for a few weeks of backpacking in late summer; reminded him to bring enough pills and keep them with him.

documents.title: Viral load
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news: your viral load dropped from 55,000 to 140 in two months, and the CD4 is holding at 362. Liver tests normal again. This is exactly the direction we want. Copy sent to the ID clinic. Have a good trip, and don't skip doses on the road.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request from pharmacy for isoniazid 300 mg and vitamin B6 50 mg, #30 each. Month 3 of 9. Approved per PCP standing plan. ART refilled on schedule last week per fill history.

reports.text: Noncontrast axial images of the head. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass lesion or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are normal in size for age; no hydrocephalus. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Basal cisterns patent. Calvarium and visualized sinuses unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No mass lesion or hydrocephalus. No acute intracranial abnormality. Safe to proceed with lumbar puncture from an imaging standpoint.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 10/15/2023

CC: headache x3 wks

HPI: 33 yo M with HIV on bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF since April and latent TB on INH, sent in by a friend. About three weeks of headache that keeps getting worse, low-grade fevers on and off, and trouble focusing at work; now and then his vision blurs. It started a few days after he got back from several weeks of backpacking in the Pacific Northwest, staying in hostels and hiking in forest. Down about 5 kg in the past month. Admits he ran out of pills partway through the trip and went a few weeks without ART before refilling.

PMH: HIV (dx 4/2023), latent TB, remote vivax malaria. PSH: appendectomy.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, isoniazid 300 mg, pyridoxine 50 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: aid worker. Former smoker, no EtOH. Remote IVDU.
FH: father HTN, mother DM2.

Exam: afebrile here, vitals otherwise per flowsheet. Alert, oriented x3 but slow to answer. Mild neck stiffness on flexion. Fundi: bilateral disc swelling, papilledema. Pupils equal and reactive, EOM full, no focal weakness, gait not tested. Lungs clear, heart regular. No rash.

CT head without contrast: no mass, no hydrocephalus.
LP (see procedure note): opening pressure elevated; fluid clear. Cell count lymphocyte predominant, protein high, glucose low for serum. India ink: encapsulated yeast. CSF crypto Ag positive 1:1024.

Impression: cryptococcal meningitis in HIV with raised intracranial pressure.
Plan: ID consulted from the ED. Liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine started. Therapeutic LP as needed for pressure. Admit to medicine.

documents.title: Lumbar puncture
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER — PROCEDURE NOTE
Date: 10/15/2023
Procedure: lumbar puncture. Indication: suspected meningitis, CT head without mass. Consent obtained. Left lateral decubitus, L3-4 interspace, sterile prep, 1% lidocaine, 20G spinal needle, clear CSF on first pass. Opening pressure elevated. Fluid removed for studies and to relieve pressure. No complications. Tubes to lab for cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain, India ink, cryptococcal antigen and fungal culture.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/15/2023, discharged 10/30/2023
Attending: hospital medicine; consultant: infectious disease

Diagnosis: cryptococcal meningitis (C. neoformans) with elevated intracranial pressure, in HIV-1 infection with CD4 170.
Other: HIV-1, viral load 3,400 after a gap in ART during travel; latent TB on isoniazid.

Course: Presented with three weeks of headache, low-grade fevers, slowed thinking and blurred vision, 5 kg weight loss. CT head without mass or hydrocephalus. CSF lymphocytic with high protein and low glucose, India ink positive, CSF cryptococcal antigen 1:1024; fungal culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans. Treated with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine for a two-week induction. Needed repeat therapeutic lumbar punctures in the first week for pressure; headache and papilledema improved, mentation back to baseline by day 6. Renal function and potassium monitored closely on amphotericin and stayed acceptable with supplementation; counts stable on flucytosine. ART continued throughout per ID, with adherence counseling. Isoniazid and pyridoxine continued.

Discharge exam: alert, fully oriented, normal speech, no neck stiffness, no focal deficits.

Discharge medications:
- fluconazole 400 mg by mouth daily (consolidation, NEW)
- trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS 1 tab daily (PJP prophylaxis, CD4 <200, NEW)
- bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily (continue)
- isoniazid 300 mg daily (continue)
- pyridoxine 50 mg daily (continue)
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: ID clinic in 2 weeks; primary care within 1 week; return for worsening headache, vision change, confusion or fever.

documents.title: Admission notification
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Call from the regional medical center case manager: pt admitted overnight from their ED, being treated for meningitis. Asked that PCP be listed as primary care on their record and that records be sent on discharge. Routed to PCP and RN.

documents.title: RE: Admission notification
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with the inpatient team. Cryptococcal meningitis on CSF, induction started, ID on board. Gave them his recent viral load and CD4 from June and his med list. Will see him within a week of discharge.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt two days after discharge. Discharge summary received and scanned. He is home, a friend is staying with him this week. Mild tiredness, no headache since the weekend, no fever, vision clear. Has fluconazole and TMP-SMX filled, along with his HIV pill, INH and B6; reviewed each, he has a pill box now. Confirmed visit Friday 11/3 at 2:00 and ID on 11/14.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after a 15-day admission 10/15 to 10/30 for cryptococcal meningitis. Discharge summary reviewed in full.

He feels a lot better. No headache in a week. Thinking is clear, reading again without trouble. Vision normal. Appetite back, weight up a little since discharge. No fevers. Some fatigue in the afternoons. Owns that he let the ART lapse on the trip and is embarrassed about it; using a weekly pill box and phone alarm now.

Meds reconciled with the discharge list: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily; fluconazole 400 mg daily (new); TMP-SMX DS daily (new, CD4 170 in hospital); isoniazid 300 mg and B6 50 mg (INH course ends late January). NKDA.

Exam: alert, oriented, fluent, good recall of the hospital course. No meningismus. Pupils equal, EOM full, no nystagmus, face symmetric, strength and gait normal. Fundi not well seen without dilation. Heart and lungs normal. Small healed bruise at the low back LP site, no tenderness.

A/P
1. Cryptococcal meningitis, after induction, on fluconazole 400 mg. Clinically back to baseline. ID visit 11/14 is the key next step; they will set the fluconazole plan. Warning signs reviewed: return of headache, vision change, confusion.
2. HIV-1 with CD4 170 at admission after an adherence gap. Back on daily ART. TMP-SMX for PJP prophylaxis. BMP and CBC today for renal function and counts on the new meds.
3. Latent TB on INH, month 7, tolerating.
4. Flu and updated COVID vaccines given today.
RTC late January when the INH course finishes, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Infectious Disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 11/14/2023

Seen two weeks after discharge for cryptococcal meningitis (C. neoformans, CSF CrAg 1:1024, final culture confirmed) treated with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine induction.

Doing well, headache resolved, no visual complaints, back at part-time work. Reports full adherence to ART since discharge; pill box in use.

Exam: normal mental status, no meningismus, no focal findings.

Plan:
1. Cryptococcal meningitis: continue fluconazole 400 mg daily.
2. HIV: continue bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF. Repeat VL and CD4 with your January labs.
3. Continue TMP-SMX DS daily until CD4 has been above 200 for at least 3 months on suppressed viral load.
4. INH: finish the 9-month course.
Return here in 4 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: MA
